title: Isola Coast: link houses turned to face the water.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #423 | ISOLA COAST, SENIBONG COVE
excerpt: The final phase of the island precinct in Senibong Cove, 160 waterfront strata homes on canals fed by the sea. Sean admires how every layer, from master plan to window, responds to the site, but flags the main road, years of works opposite and a price that only makes sense on site.
takeaways: Freehold 22 by 110 ft link houses with the living space at the back, facing the water, from about RM2.6 million.
Canals, a marina and dense landscaping make the setting the real product.
The Sembawang shipyard opposite is due to move, but reclamation and building works will run for years.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Isola Coast is the last phase of the Isola island precinct in the 250-acre Senibong Cove township: 160 strata landed homes along canals fed by the sea, in link houses, cluster homes and bungalows of about RM3 to RM4 million. The landscaping is planted before handover, with fine-leaved trees that screen each home from the street.

The freehold link house is 22 by 110 ft and turns the usual layout around: a large entrance and foyer at the front, a courtyard in the middle, and the kitchen, dining and living room at the back, 6.3 m wide and almost all glass, facing the water. There is a ground-floor bedroom and a helper's room, three en-suite bedrooms above, a junior suite on the top floor and a rooftop terrace.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: Senibong Cove sits on the Johor Strait opposite Sembawang in Singapore, about 12 km from the Woodlands checkpoint, reached from the main road between JB and Masai. AEON is less than 10 minutes away, and the township has its own marina and a retail village with restaurants and events. In front, 166 acres are being reclaimed for the next precinct, and Singapore has announced plans to relocate the Sembawang shipyard.

standout.title: Windows placed for the house to breathe
standout.body: Windows cover almost every bit of the facade facing the water, and the openings line up with the central courtyard so air can cross the whole house. Even the ground-floor bedroom's window sits high, at about 1.76 m, so it lets in light and air without exposing the room to the car porch or passers-by.

pros: The site: seafront, estuary and mangroves only about 12 km from Woodlands, a setting few places offer, best suited to raising a family, a holiday home, or somewhere to host family, friends and business partners, with room to moor a yacht.

A design approach that follows the site from master plan to unit: a marina where the water is calm, lush landscaping to match the mangroves, canals that bring the water to more homes, shared decks along the edge, and now apartments too, with Hill View starting at about RM750 psf, around RM420,000.

Attention to detail: trees that screen the houses from the street, hidden substations and refuse areas, and a layout that puts living space at the back without losing a generous entrance, a ground-floor bedroom or a rooftop for entertaining. His favourite feature is the placement and scale of the windows.
cons: The township relies on the congested main road between Masai and the city at peak hours, though the developer runs shuttles to Singapore, which suits someone who only goes into the office once or twice a week.

The Sembawang shipyard opposite: its relocation has been announced, but with the reclamation in front it will take five to eight years for the view to settle, and empty mansion lots next door could start building at any time.

On paper the price is hard to justify, since RM2.6 million buys many other options nearer JB city. Sean says you are paying for the setting rather than the built-up, and urges buyers to visit the site to feel the difference.

closing: A family home built around the water rather than its square footage; Sean loves it but says the apartments are his only way in.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this January 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team showed Sean the site and the show unit; prices are as he quoted them. Sean doesn't discuss rents for this phase, so none are given.
